material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted interior surfaces. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings. Primary RP primer for sound-to-peeling conditions where adhesion enhancement is needed.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime all scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional — skip if adhesion test passes on low-sheen surfaces; apply if marginal adhesion or high-sheen existing finish or oil-based base identified
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas (<30% bare) or full prime (>=30% bare)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime — extensive bare area after complete scrape

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac-Based)
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain blocker for smoke damage, nicotine, soot, and severe water stains. Full-surface application required — spot treatment insufficient because smoke contamination is pervasive even when not visually apparent. Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required — pervasive contamination means spot treatment fails. Strong odor — requires ventilation (open windows, fans). Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup — requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Fire-safe handling required (flammable solvent base).

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged surfaces. Applied after biocide treatment (bleach/mildewcide) and full drying. Prevents mildew regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting.

products.notes: Apply only after biocide treatment and full drying (24+ hrs). Contains antimicrobial additives that prevent spore regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: active moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades before painting. Painting over active moisture is cosmetic-only and fails within weeks.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface prime on all affected walls — mildew spores not visible to naked eye may be present beyond visible damage

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Standard Interior Wall Finish (QT2-QT3)
material_systems.description: Standard 100% acrylic latex wall paint for economy and standard residential repaint. Same product class as NC wall finish. Good coverage, washability, and durability for residential use.

products.notes: QT2: 1 finish coat over primed surface is acceptable (economy tier). QT3: 2 finish coats default, 1 acceptable if full coverage achieved. Eggshell is default residential wall sheen. Flat/matte for ceiling-adjacent or low-traffic areas. Actual coat count specified in PaintScope, not derived from QT.

material_systems.name: Premium Interior Wall Finish (QT4)
material_systems.description: Premium 100% acrylic wall paint with superior leveling, hide, and durability. Better flow and self-leveling reduces brush marks and roller stipple. Required at QT4 for satin sheen due to higher sheen revealing imperfections.

products.notes: QT4: 2 finish coats mandatory. Full sand between coats at QT4+ (220 grit). Satin available at QT4+ — requires enhanced prep to prevent sheen-revealed imperfections. Premium paint provides better leveling that reduces brush and roller marks.

material_systems.name: Superior Interior Wall Finish (QT5)
material_systems.description: Top-tier interior wall paint with maximum hide, leveling, and durability. Showroom-quality appearance. Required for semi-gloss walls due to magnified imperfection visibility at high sheen.

products.notes: QT5: 2 finish coats mandatory. Full sand between ALL coats (primer-to-finish and between finish coats, 220 grit). Semi-gloss available only at QT5 — magnifies every imperfection, requires meticulous workmanship and controlled environment. Critical inspection at every stage.

sheen_quality_tier_rules.description: Sheen availability is quality-tier restricted per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md

rules.notes: Lower sheens hide imperfections; available at any quality tier
Satin reveals imperfections; requires enhanced prep and sanding discipline
Semi-gloss magnifies imperfections; requires meticulous workmanship

sheen_quality_tier_rules.automatic_upgrade_rule: If specified sheen exceeds quality tier maximum, automatically upgrade quality tier per doctrine
sheen_quality_tier_rules.gloss_note: Gloss is NOT available for drywall walls. Gloss on drywall is not a real-world application.

coat_count_defaults.description: Default coat counts by quality tier. Actual coat count is specified in PaintScope and may differ from defaults.

primer_coats.description: Primer coat count is state-driven, not QT-driven.
primer_coats.notes: All 3 primer systems require exactly 1 coat. A second primer coat is a failure-mode indicator (insufficient coverage on first coat) — not a quality upgrade.

QT2.notes: Economy tier. 1 coat acceptable over primed surface. 2 coats if color change is dramatic or coverage insufficient.

QT3.notes: Standard residential. 2 coats for uniform color depth and hide. 1 coat acceptable if full coverage achieved on first coat.

QT4.notes: Premium tier. 2 coats mandatory with full sand between coats.

QT5.notes: Showroom tier. 2 coats mandatory with full sand between all coats and critical inspection.

coat_count_defaults.important: Coat count is NOT derived from quality tier. These are spec defaults only. Actual coat count comes from PaintScope specification. QT2 requiring 2 coats does NOT bump to QT3.

SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT.notes: Sound existing paint. Low porosity — primer sits on surface. Full surface or spot application.

SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Mixed surface — some bare drywall exposed after scraping. Bare areas absorb more primer.

SS_INT_PEELING.notes: Mostly bare after full scrape. Higher primer consumption on exposed drywall substrate.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Previously painted smooth drywall. Coverage is for affected area only on spot prime; for full wall SF on full prime. Bare drywall areas absorb ~15% more primer than sound paint.

SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT.notes: Textured sound paint. Texture valleys absorb more primer.

SS_INT_PEELING.notes: Textured mostly bare surface. Highest primer consumption.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Textured drywall wall (orange peel, knockdown, or heavy texture). Texture increases surface area, reducing coverage 10-20% vs smooth.

SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE.notes: Shellac on smooth smoke-damaged wall. Full surface application mandatory. Shellac coverage slightly lower than latex primers due to thinner film build.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Smooth previously painted wall with smoke/nicotine contamination. Shellac dries thin — coverage is per manufacturer PDS (BIN: 350-400 SF/gal). Full surface coverage required.

SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE.notes: Shellac on textured smoke-damaged wall. Texture valleys require more material for complete seal.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Textured wall with smoke contamination. Coverage reduced 15-20% vs smooth due to texture.

SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE.notes: Mildew-resistant primer on smooth moisture-damaged wall. Applied after biocide treatment and drying. Coverage similar to standard latex primer.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Smooth wall after biocide treatment. Surface has been cleaned and dried. Coverage comparable to standard latex primer.

SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE.notes: Textured moisture-damaged wall. Texture increases material consumption.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Textured wall after biocide treatment and drying.
Primed or sound-paint wall surface, smooth texture. Coverage rates match NC wall finish — once surface is properly prepped and primed, finish coat behavior is identical. Per-coat coverage.
Orange peel texture increases surface area, reduces coverage ~12% vs smooth.
Knockdown texture increases surface area, reduces coverage ~18% vs smooth.
Heavy texture (stomp, skip trowel) significantly increases surface area. ~30% coverage reduction vs smooth. skip_trowel treated as heavy_texture per research.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Chemical Degloss
consumables.specification: Liquid sander deglosser (e.g., Krud Kutter Gloss-Off, Jasco Liquid Sander, Klean-Strip Easy Liquid Sander)
consumables.notes: Chemical degloss for RP adhesion prep. Wipe-on application removes gloss sheen without mechanical sanding. Faster than mechanical scuff (~200-300 SF/hr vs 150-250 SF/hr). Allow 10-15 min dry time before coating. Alternative to mechanical degloss with 120-150 grit. Not needed on POOR condition (surface already scraped to bare).

consumables.name: TSP Powder (Trisodium Phosphate)
consumables.specification: Trisodium phosphate powder, 1 lb box (mix ~1/4 cup per gallon water)
consumables.notes: Surface cleaning for grease film, kitchen residue, smoke residue, and general contamination. Required before degloss or coating application. Mix per manufacturer directions. Rinse after wash. Wear gloves — TSP is caustic. TSP substitutes (TSP-PF) acceptable where phosphate restrictions apply.

consumables.name: Bleach / Mildewcide Solution
consumables.specification: Household bleach (sodium hypochlorite 5-8%) diluted 1:3 with water, or commercial mildewcide concentrate
consumables.notes: Biocide treatment for mildew-affected areas. Apply with spray bottle or sponge, allow 15-30 min dwell time for full kill, rinse thoroughly, allow 24+ hrs drying. Mildew spores must be killed before priming — painting over live mildew results in regrowth through paint film. Ventilation required.

consumables.name: Denatured Alcohol (Shellac Cleanup)
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol, 1 quart
consumables.notes: Required for shellac stain-blocker tool cleanup. SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT uses shellac — standard water cleanup does NOT work. Approximately 1 QT denatured alcohol per 5 GAL of shellac primer used. Flammable — store and handle per OSHA requirements. Dispose of solvent-soaked rags properly to prevent spontaneous combustion.

consumables.name: Adhesion Test Kit (ASTM D3359)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter and pressure-sensitive tape per ASTM D3359 Method B
consumables.notes: Used during assessment phase for all RP projects. Cross-hatch cut through existing coating, apply tape, pull at 180 degrees, evaluate adhesion grade (0B-5B). One test per representative area plus suspect zones. Kit includes cutter blade and tape rolls. ~100 tests per kit.

consumables.name: Poly Sheeting for Furniture Protection (2-4 mil)
consumables.specification: Polyethylene sheeting, 2-4 mil, 10 ft wide roll
consumables.notes: Furniture covering in occupied homes. Center-pile furniture and drape with poly. Tape edges to floor to prevent paint migration under sheeting. 2 mil minimum, 4 mil for spray methods. One roll covers approximately 400 SF of draped area.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80 grit
consumables.specification: 80 grit sandpaper for pole sander or hand sanding
consumables.notes: For heavy degloss and feathering scraped edges on FAIR/POOR condition walls. Aggressive grit for removing thick paint ridges and smoothing transitions from scraped to sound paint areas. 25 SF per sheet for heavy work.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120 grit
consumables.specification: 120 grit sandpaper for pole sander or hand sanding
consumables.notes: For mechanical degloss (scuff sanding) as alternative to chemical degloss. Also for refining feathered edges after initial 80-grit work. 120 grit is the standard mechanical degloss grit for RP.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 grit
consumables.specification: 150 grit sandpaper for pole sander
consumables.notes: Fine-grit mechanical degloss for lighter scuff sanding. Suitable for walls where 120 grit is too aggressive. Also for feathering on thin-film existing coatings.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit
consumables.specification: 220 grit sandpaper for pole sander
consumables.notes: For sanding between finish coats at QT4+. Full sand per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md Sanding Standards. Also for sanding between primer and finish coat at QT5. 220 grit is the standard interstage sanding grit.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle
consumables.specification: Lightweight vinyl spackle, premixed
consumables.notes: For filling nail holes, small dings, minor surface defects, and scrape-edge transitions before priming. Lightweight spackle for shallow fills (under 1/8 inch). Deep fills require setting-type compound. ~100 spot fills per quart.

consumables.name: Paintable latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: For resealing trim-to-wall joints that have cracked or separated. Common in RP where building movement has opened gaps since original caulking. ~30 LF per tube at standard bead width.

consumables.name: 3-inch putty knife
consumables.specification: 3-inch flexible putty knife, stainless or carbon steel
consumables.notes: For scraping loose and peeling paint. 3-inch width for targeted scraping at moderate scale. Also used for spackle application. Long tool life.

consumables.name: 6-inch drywall/paint scraper
consumables.specification: 6-inch wide scraper with replaceable blade
consumables.notes: For large-area scraping on POOR condition walls (peeling, widespread failure). 6-inch width for production scraping. Replaceable blade for efficiency.

consumables.name: Pole sander
consumables.specification: Pole sander head for extension pole
consumables.notes: Pole sander for wall sanding — mechanical degloss, feathering, and interstage sanding between coats (QT4+). Attaches to extension pole for full-height wall access without ladder.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Tack cloth, standard size
consumables.notes: For dust removal after sanding before coating application. Critical at QT4+ where sanding dust trapped under finish coat creates visible defects. One tack cloth per ~200 SF of sanded surface.

consumables.name: 9-inch roller cover, 3/8" to 1/2" nap
consumables.specification: 9-inch standard roller cover, 3/8 to 1/2 inch nap range, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: Standard 9-inch roller for roll-only method. 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth AND textured walls (orange peel, knockdown). Do NOT use 3/4" nap for orange peel or knockdown — 3/4" is only for stomp/popcorn or porous masonry. Replace per product change or after ~5000 SF.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller cover, 3/8" to 1/2" nap
consumables.specification: 18-inch production roller cover, 3/8 to 1/2 inch nap range, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: 18-inch roller for spray+backroll production. 3/8" to 1/2" nap for all standard drywall textures. 18-inch is standard/preferred but not mandatory — 9-inch may be required for tight spaces.

consumables.name: 9-inch roller frame
consumables.specification: 9-inch standard roller frame with threaded handle
consumables.notes: Standard 9-inch frame for roll-only or as backup for tight spaces during spray+backroll.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller frame
consumables.specification: 18-inch production roller frame with threaded handle
consumables.notes: 18-inch frame for production spray+backroll. Not mandatory — 9-inch may be required for tight spaces.

consumables.name: Extension pole
consumables.specification: Telescoping extension pole, 4-8 ft adjustable
consumables.notes: For wall rolling and backrolling at standard and tall heights. Also used with pole sander for degloss/interstage sanding.

consumables.name: 2.5-inch angled sash brush
consumables.specification: 2.5-inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Used for ceiling-line edge cut-in and trim-adjacent cut-in. Wall painter establishes ceiling line and cuts to tape line at trim. Synthetic bristle for latex paint. ~3000 LF with proper care. Separate brush recommended for primer vs finish.

consumables.name: Paint tray
consumables.specification: Standard 9-inch paint tray with liner
consumables.notes: Tray with disposable liner for roll method.

consumables.name: Paint tray liner
consumables.specification: Disposable plastic tray liner
consumables.notes: Replace each session or product change.

consumables.name: 5-gallon bucket with grid
consumables.specification: 5-gallon bucket with roller grid
consumables.notes: Standard for production spray+backroll wall work.

consumables.name: Spray tip 517 (primer)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 517 (10-inch fan, 0.017 orifice)
consumables.notes: Standard tip for primer on drywall walls. Larger orifice than finish tips for thicker primer viscosity. Use for all 3 primer systems (adhesion, stain-block, mildew). For shellac primer (BIN), dedicated tip recommended — do not share with latex.

consumables.name: Spray tip 415 (finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 415 (8-inch fan, 0.015 orifice)
consumables.notes: Standard tip for wall finish paint. Smaller fan and orifice than primer tips for better atomization on finish coats.

consumables.name: Spray tip 413 (fine finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 413 (8-inch fan, 0.013 orifice)
consumables.notes: Fine atomization tip for QT4+ finish coats. Finer orifice than 415 for smoother finish. May require thinning of heavier-body paints.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. Dedicated filter when switching between shellac and latex — do not cross-contaminate.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft, 8 oz weight
consumables.notes: Reusable floor perimeter protection for roll method. Positioned along base of walls being rolled. Canvas absorbs drips and prevents slip hazard on finished floors.

consumables.name: Rosin paper
consumables.specification: Red rosin paper, 36-inch wide roll
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for hard floors during wall spray. Taped seams required per Protection_and_Masking_Doctrine. RP always has finished floors.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 1.5 mil (floor protection)
consumables.specification: 1.5 mil plastic sheeting for floor protection
consumables.notes: Full floor coverage for carpet during wall spray. Taped edges required.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 14-day clean removal
consumables.notes: Standard blue tape for trim edge masking, floor seams, fixture covers, general protection. 180 LF (60 yards) per roll. RP always requires trim masking — this is the primary masking consumable.

consumables.name: Green edge-seal tape
consumables.specification: Green edge-seal painter's tape (e.g., Frog Tape), 1.5-inch width
consumables.notes: Green edge-seal tape for crisp paint lines at QT4+. Requires damp rag edge seal per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine tape technique. Premium cost justified at QT4+ where edge quality is critical.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: 12-inch masking paper for fixture and trim protection
consumables.notes: 12-inch paper attached to blue tape for extended trim and fixture protection during spray. Covers exposed trim face below tape line.

consumables.name: Pre-taped masking film
consumables.specification: Pre-taped plastic masking film, 24-48 inch width
consumables.notes: Pre-taped film for quick masking of windows, doors, and large trim areas during spray application. Faster to apply than separate tape + paper.

consumables.name: Outlet/switch covers (masking)
consumables.specification: Plastic fixture covers or masking film squares for outlets/switches
consumables.notes: Covers for electrical outlets and switches during spray. Estimate ~6 per room average via PS_META.EA.ROOMS_TOTAL heuristic. Also recommended for roll at QT4+ to prevent drip contamination.

consumption_models.description: Primer material quantity based on wall field area, primer system, and prime scope (spot vs full)
consumption_models.notes: Affected area varies by state: spot prime = scraped area only (bare_percentage * wall_field_sf); full prime = wall_field_sf. Select coverage profile based on primer system, substrate state, and surface texture. Add 5-10% waste factor for spray methods.

consumption_models.description: Finish paint material quantity based on wall field area and coat count
consumption_models.notes: Select coverage profile based on finish system and surface texture. Coat count from PaintScope specification (defaults by QT if not specified). Add 5-10% waste factor for spray methods. RP coverage rates match NC — once surface is primed, finish behavior is identical.
1 brush per material type minimum. Separate brush for primer and finish recommended. Wall painter establishes ceiling line via freehand cut-in.

consumption_models.description: Brush for trim-adjacent cut-in (RP-specific — trim always in place)
consumption_models.notes: Cut-in at trim edges where tape line provides the target. Uses same brush as ceiling cut-in (CON_BRUSH_ANGLED_2_5IN). Brush consumption shared across ceiling and trim cut-in.

consumption_models.description: Roller cover replacement based on wall area and coat count
consumption_models.notes: Driven by product count and color count per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine. Use 3/8" to 1/2" nap for all standard wall textures. Separate covers for primer and finish.

consumption_models.description: Floor protection material for spray/spray_backroll methods
consumption_models.notes: Rosin paper for hard floors, plastic sheeting for carpet. Material selection driven by floor_type site condition. RP always has finished floors.

consumption_models.description: Floor protection (perimeter drops) for roll method
consumption_models.formula: Reusable drop cloths positioned along wall perimeter.
consumption_models.notes: Canvas drops for roll method. Less material than spray full-floor coverage.

consumption_models.description: Tape for masking trim edges before wall work. RP always has trim in place — this is mandatory.
consumption_models.notes: Blue tape standard at QT2-QT3; green edge-seal tape at QT4+ for crisp lines. Tape applied before prep phase and remains through finish. RP spec OWNS trim masking — trim is always in place.

consumption_models.description: Poly sheeting for furniture protection in occupied homes
consumption_models.notes: Poly sheeting for center-piled furniture. Conditional on occupancy_state. Not needed for vacant RP.

consumption_models.description: Sandpaper for between-coat sanding at QT4+
consumption_models.notes: Full sand between coats at QT4+ only. 220 grit per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md Sanding Standards.
Chemical degloss when mechanical sanding is not preferred. Conditional on method selection (chemical vs mechanical degloss). Coverage ~200 SF per quart.
TSP wash for contaminated surfaces. Coverage ~500 SF per 1 lb box. Conditional on contamination_type.
Bleach/mildewcide for SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE areas. Coverage ~300 SF per gallon diluted solution. Conditional on substrate_state.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint, adhesion passes, low sheen — no primer required
compatibility_rules.notes: GOOD condition with passing adhesion test and low-sheen existing finish. Direct finish coat application acceptable. Most economical RP pathway.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint, high sheen or marginal adhesion — adhesion primer required

when.conditions: adhesion_test marginal OR existing_sheen in [satin, semi-gloss, gloss] OR coating_id = oil_based

compatibility_rules.notes: High-sheen existing paint or marginal adhesion test results require adhesion primer even on sound paint. Oil-based existing coating requires adhesion primer for latex topcoat compatibility.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint <30% bare — spot adhesion prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Spot prime all scraped and feathered areas. Adhesion primer bonds to both bare drywall and remaining sound paint.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint >=30% bare — full adhesion prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Extensive bare exposure. Full prime prevents flashing/sheen variance from differential absorption between bare and sound areas.

compatibility_rules.description: Peeling — full adhesion prime after complete scrape
compatibility_rules.notes: Full scrape to sound substrate followed by full adhesion prime. Extensive bare area after peeling paint removal.

compatibility_rules.description: Moisture damage — mildew-resistant primer after biocide treatment
compatibility_rules.notes: Gate condition: moisture source MUST be resolved first. Biocide treatment kills existing mildew. Mildew-resistant primer prevents regrowth. Full surface prime on all affected walls.

compatibility_rules.description: Smoke damage — shellac stain blocker, full surface, no exceptions
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface — spot treatment fails because contamination is pervasive. Latex primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

compatibility_rules.description: Sheen-QT gate: satin requires QT4+, semi-gloss requires QT5
compatibility_rules.constraint: Flat/matte/eggshell at any QT; satin at QT4+; semi-gloss at QT5 only; gloss NOT available for drywall walls
compatibility_rules.notes: Per Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md. If specified sheen exceeds QT maximum, auto-upgrade QT.

compatibility_rules.description: Roller nap selection for drywall walls
compatibility_rules.constraint: Use 3/8" to 1/2" nap for smooth, orange peel, and knockdown textures. Do NOT use 3/4" nap for orange peel or knockdown.
compatibility_rules.notes: 3/4" nap is only appropriate for very porous concrete, stomp texture, or popcorn ceilings. Per resolved doctrine conflict DC-001.

compatibility_rules.description: Latex finish compatible with all 3 RP primer systems
compatibility_rules.constraint: All finish systems (standard/premium/superior) are 100% acrylic latex and are fully compatible with adhesion primer (latex), mildew-resistant primer (latex), and shellac stain-blocker (topcoat with latex after cure).
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac primer requires 45+ min cure before latex topcoat. All other primers are latex-to-latex direct compatibility.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac primer requires dedicated cleanup and spray equipment

then.equipment_note: Dedicated spray tip for shellac — do not share with latex

compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac primer uses denatured alcohol solvent base. Cannot be cleaned with water. Dedicated spray tip prevents cross-contamination of shellac residue into latex equipment.

compatibility_rules.description: Pre-1978 with paint disturbance — RRP lead-safe supplies required
compatibility_rules.notes: EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745). Pre-1978 homes with paint disturbance (scraping, sanding) require lead-safe work practices. Interior walls are common lead paint substrate. Consumables defined in shared MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT module.

risk_notes.description: Adhesion failure over existing semi-gloss or gloss paint when degloss is insufficient or adhesion primer is skipped.
risk_notes.mitigation: Thorough degloss (liquid sander or mechanical scuff), adhesion test before proceeding, adhesion primer when sheen is semi-gloss or higher or when coating ID shows oil-based base.

risk_notes.description: Stain bleed-through from smoke, nicotine, or water damage when using latex primer instead of shellac stain blocker.
risk_notes.mitigation: Proper contamination identification during assessment phase. Shellac-based stain blocker (BIN) mandatory for smoke damage. Latex/acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

risk_notes.description: Mildew regrowth through new paint film when painting over live mildew without biocide treatment.
risk_notes.mitigation: Biocide treatment during prep, full dry time, mildew-resistant primer. Moisture source must be resolved before painting — HARD GATE.

risk_notes.description: Latex finish applied directly over oil/alkyd base without adhesion primer — peeling occurs within weeks.
risk_notes.mitigation: Coating identification in assessment phase (solvent test). Adhesion primer mandatory when oil-based existing coating identified.

risk_notes.description: Shellac stain-blocker (BIN) is flammable solvent-based product. Fire risk during application and cleanup. Strong odor in occupied home.
risk_notes.mitigation: Ventilation required (open windows, fans). No open flames or ignition sources. Proper disposal of solvent-soaked rags. Occupants should vacate during application and for 2+ hours after.

risk_notes.description: Flashing/sheen variance where scraped areas meet sound paint due to differential absorption.
risk_notes.mitigation: Feather-sand all scrape edges. Full prime when bare area exceeds 30% of wall. Consistent primer film build across entire surface.

risk_notes.description: Paint spatter or contact damage to furniture/belongings in occupied home.
risk_notes.mitigation: Center-pile furniture 4+ ft from walls, full poly sheeting cover, tape edges to floor. Special attention to fabric furniture and electronics. High liability for irreplaceable items.

risk_notes.description: Lap marks on wall finish coat when wet edge is not maintained. More visible at higher sheens.
risk_notes.mitigation: Maintain wet edge during application. Work in sections. Spray+backroll reduces lap mark risk vs roll-only.

assumptions.value: Adhesion primer: 350-400 SF/gal smooth, adjusted for texture. Shellac: 300-350 SF/gal. Mildew-resistant: 300-350 SF/gal.
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS (BIN, Stix, KILZ) and sibling NC wall primer spec
assumptions.note: Coverage rates derived from manufacturer product data sheets and NC wall primer coverage rates adjusted for RP conditions (existing paint vs bare drywall).

assumptions.value: Same as NC wall finish: 400 SF/gal smooth, adjusted for texture
assumptions.note: Once surface is primed, finish coat behavior is identical between NC and RP. Coverage rates transfer directly.
No doctrine coverage for spray waste factor. RP spray waste may be slightly higher than NC due to occupied-home masking complexity.

assumptions.value: RP wall spec owns trim masking task — trim is always in place
assumptions.note: NC wall prime could skip trim masking (trim not installed). RP cannot — trim is always present and must be masked before any wall work.

assumptions.value: Poly sheeting covers center-piled furniture at ~400 SF per roll
assumptions.note: No doctrine for furniture protection material quantities. Estimated from practical coverage of 2-4 mil poly sheeting draped over center-piled furniture.

assumptions.value: Chemical degloss (liquid sander) is preferred for RP; mechanical scuff is alternative
assumptions.note: No doctrine specifying preference between chemical and mechanical degloss. Chemical is faster but adds dry time. Both methods produce acceptable results.

uncertainty_flags.description: Liquid sander coverage rate (~200 SF/qt) is estimated from manufacturer guidance. Actual coverage varies by application method (wipe vs spray) and surface porosity.
Mildewcide solution coverage (~300 SF/gal diluted) is estimated. Actual varies by severity of mildew contamination and application method.

Spray tip selection for shellac primer (BIN) may differ from latex primer tips. Shellac has different viscosity and atomization characteristics. Manufacturer recommends 515-617 range but field practice may vary.
Furniture protection poly sheeting quantity is estimated per room. Actual depends on furniture density and room layout. No PaintScope key currently captures furniture density.

research_corrections.title: Latex/acrylic primers have zero stain blocking capability
research_corrections.impact: Shellac stain-blocker (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT) is the ONLY option for smoke damage. No latex primer substitute.

research_corrections.title: Do not specify dry times in specs
research_corrections.impact: No dry time references in materials — refer to manufacturer PDS. Exception: mildew treatment requires 24+ hr drying note as a gate condition.

research_corrections.title: Gloss not available for drywall walls
research_corrections.impact: No gloss finish system. Gloss on drywall is not a real-world application.

research_corrections.title: Semi-gloss gated at QT5 only
research_corrections.impact: SYS_WALL_FINISH_SUPERIOR (QT5) is the only system with semi-gloss availability.
